title: Energetics Decomposition of Sac7d:DNA Decrypts Amino Acids Role Without DNA Sequence Selectivity.
authors: Alvarez-Sanchez, Elena; Offmann, Bernard; Huet, Simon; Teletchea, Stephane
one_liner_zh: 该文通过1微秒分子动力学模拟和MM/GBSA能量分解，解析Sac7d蛋白与DNA小沟的非序列特异性结合机制，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Sac7d is a 7 kDa protein belonging to the class of the small chromosomal proteins from archeon Sulfolobus acidocaldarius. Sac7d was discovered in 1974 in Yellowstone National Parks geysers, and studied extensively since then for its remarkable stability at large pH and temperature ranges. Sac7d binds to the DNA minor groove, thereby protecting the host genome from extreme conditions by increasing the DNA melting temperature. In this study, we analyzed the Sac7d-DNA complex using 1 mus molecular dynamics simulations. The interaction energy of the interface was decomposed using Molecular Mechanics with Generalized Born Surface Area (MM/GBSA) to determine the residues that contributed most significantly to DNA binding. Out of 12 amino acids considered essential for DNA binding, three were newly identified in this study and had not been previously reported. One of these new amino acids, R63, may be involved in a dynamic protein-DNA interaction. The simulations performed also revealed a sliding motion of Sac7d over double-stranded DNA, suggesting a minimal sequence dependence interaction. Our analysis thus provides novel insights into how the Sac7d chaperones allow to protect DNA from degradation in extreme conditions.
abstract_zh: Sac7d是一种7 kDa的蛋白质，属于来自嗜酸热硫化叶菌（Sulfolobus acidocaldarius）的小染色体蛋白类别。Sac7d于1974年在黄石国家公园的间歇泉中被发现，此后因其在广泛pH和温度范围内的显著稳定性而被广泛研究。Sac7d结合DNA小沟，通过提高DNA熔解温度来保护宿主基因组免受极端条件的影响。在本研究中，我们使用1微秒的分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟分析了Sac7d-DNA复合物。通过广义Born表面积分子力学 (MM/GBSA) 方法分解了界面的相互作用能，以确定对DNA结合贡献最显著的残基。在12个被认为对DNA结合至关重要的氨基酸中，有三个是在本研究中新鉴定的，此前未见报道。其中一个新氨基酸R63可能参与动态的蛋白质-DNA相互作用。进行的模拟还揭示了Sac7d在双链DNA上的滑动运动，表明其具有极低的序列依赖性相互作用。因此，我们的分析为Sac7d伴侣蛋白如何在极端条件下保护DNA免受降解提供了新的见解。
